Class LcdKeypadShield

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.api.lcd.LcdKeypadShield
public final class LcdKeypadShield extends Object
Driver for the common "LCD Keypad Shield" (a 16x2 HD44780-compatible character LCD in 4-bit mode, plus 5 buttons wired through a single resistor ladder into one analog pin), wired for its standard pinout as used by e.g. dzindra/lcdkeypad: LCD data/control on digital pins 4-9, backlight on digital pin 10, buttons on A0.

Unlike LedMatrix, this shield needs no new compiler intrinsic: every operation here is built from Gpio.pinMode(int, int), Gpio.digitalWrite(int, boolean), Gpio.analogRead(int), and Delay, the same way LedCanvas is built from LedMatrix.

    • backlight

      public static void backlight(boolean on)
      Turns the backlight on or off. The shield's backlight LED is wired straight to this pin with no current-limiting resistor on some board revisions, so this never drives the pin HIGH: "on" writes LOW and then floats the pin (INPUT), "off" drives it LOW as an output. Driving the pin HIGH can pull down the shared 5V rail hard enough to keep the LCD itself from initializing.

    • print

      public static void print(byte[] buffer, int length)
      Prints the first length bytes of buffer as raw ASCII characters, starting at the cursor, without wrapping. Unlike print(String), this never builds a runtime String — for content that already lives in a caller-owned byte buffer (e.g. Pop3Client.readSubject(String, int, String, String, int, byte[], int)'s output) and would otherwise need a heap allocation just to be displayed.
